subject: Transportation Systems
title: Flaps and Slats
description: Learn Flaps and Slats in one minute.

hook.text: During takeoff and landing, a plane flies slowly. It needs extra lift at low speed. Enter flaps.

buildup.text: Flaps extend from the back of the wing, changing its shape to generate more lift at lower speeds.

discovery.text: Slats extend from the front, keeping airflow attached to the wing at steeper angles.

twist.text: Flaps also increase drag—useful for slowing down during approach, but costly during cruise.

climax.text: Once airborne and fast, pilots retract everything. The clean wing is optimized for cruising speed.

punchline.text: Flaps turn a fast wing into a slow-speed lifter.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of wing flaps?
options: To increase lift at low speeds
